verdicts.question: Will UIDAI register an early-stage startup as an Offline Verification Seeking Entity (OVSE), at what fee and process, and does the Aadhaar app's credential-sharing flow work from a web app or PWA rather than a native app? Should a pilot accept masked Aadhaar at all given the QR-signature check, or only driving licence, voter ID, PAN or DigiLocker documents?
verdicts.problems: Method note: WebSearch budget was exhausted and every page fetch is refused, so I verified through GitHub mirrors of the primary texts (code-search snippets), not the cited URLs. CONFIRMED by snippet from a statute mirror of the Aadhaar Regulations as amended 9 Dec 2025: Reg 13A(1)-(9) (registration on UIDAI's terms, lawful-purpose proviso, 15-day rejection notice, 30-day reconsideration, 13A(9) 'may from time to time determine the fee and charges'); Reg 2(bc) Secure QR and 2(be) Aadhaar Verifiable Credential definitions; Reg 3A (VC verification 'with or without offline face verification'); Reg 14A(b) (OVSE shall not collect, use or store Aadhaar number or biometrics); Reg 16B(1) (OVSE verifies printed details against the digitally signed Secure QR); Reg 16C(1) (no acceptance without verifying UIDAI's signature in the Secure QR on the letter, e-Aadhaar or Paperless Offline e-KYC; the 2025 amendment deleted 'm-Aadhaar' and '(XML)'); Reg 20A(1)(d) (logs 'shall not, in any event, store the Aadhaar number or Virtual ID'); Act s.29(4); Act s.40 (up to 3 years, Rs 10,000, or Rs 1 lakh for a company). CONFIRMED from a mirror of the Decentro post (27 Apr 2026): 'UIDAI charges a nominal fee', 'from application submission to go-live, can take anywhere from a few weeks to a few months'. ERRORS: (1) 'by regulatory definition carries only the last 4 digits' overstates Reg 2(be), which says the credential 'may contain last 4 digits ... and such other information as may be specified by the Authority'; drop 'only'. (2) The 'Regulation 5(3) requires that nobody is refused service' cite could not be found in the mirror; the no-denial principle sits in Act s.7 proviso/s.8 disclosure of alternatives and Reg 5(1)(c) (alternatives must be told to the holder); cite those instead. NOT CONFIRMED by any snippet (source pages not found through the alternatives): the OVSE page dates (13 May / 18 Sep 2026) and the handbook's document list (SVG under 10 KB, 2-year Class 2/3 certificate, callback URL); 'about 100 entities' (ETV Bharat) and the IAMAI onboarding; the SecuredApp post; the docs.uidai.gov.in portal-initiated journey wording (docs.uidai.gov.in exists and a third-party wallet catalogue describes the Aadhaar App's 'portable SD-JWT credential sharing', which supports the SD-JWT claim only in outline); the Aadhaar App FAQ statement that QR reading is limited to UIDAI's apps; the PIB release; the '2048-bit' figure. Note the earlier draft (answers-v1) said 200+ entities per a 20 Aug 2026 UIDAI release while this version says about 100 by April 2026; neither is confirmed, so the count should be presented as unverified. NEW FINDING the researcher missed: an OVSE integrator's public guide (OnGrid, WEBVIEW_NATIVE_APP_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md) states 'redirecting to Aadhaar app and completing Aadhaar validation as part of OVSE flow is not supported as of now' on iOS, and its token API distinguishes channel APP (app-to-app) from WEB (browser redirect); this turns the answer's 'not documented in detail' into 'reported unsupported on iOS', which strengthens the cross-device QR recommendation. Refined chain: the answer speaks of Saathis and kabadiwalas only; under the 30 Sep model the same person-check applies to the natural person (owner or authorised signatory) behind every new business role (pre-processor, compounder, DWCC/MRF operator, brand, authorised waste handler, TSDF), while the entity-level checks for those roles (GSTIN, KSPCB consent or authorisation, CPCB/KSPCB EPR registration) are a separate admin checklist and must not be conflated with ID verification.
verdicts.correction: Registration: Regulation 13A (inserted 9 Dec 2025) sets no size, age or turnover test: an entity applies on UIDAI's form and terms, must use verification only for lawful purposes, gets written grounds within 15 days if rejected and may seek reconsideration within 30 days; 13A(9) lets UIDAI set registration and per-transaction fees, and no amount is published on any official page. Decentro (27 Apr 2026) calls the fee 'nominal' and puts application-to-go-live at 'a few weeks to a few months', so registration cannot sit on the 13 Oct critical path and the fee is an open item for ovse.registration@uidai.net.in. Reports that roughly 100 to 200 private and public entities have been registered since the January 2026 rollout could not be confirmed from a snippet and should be treated as unverified colour. The application document list (PAN, incorporation certificate, company profile, self-declaration, domain, HTTPS callback URL, public certificate, SVG logo) comes from the researcher's reading of the January 2026 handbook and was not re-confirmed; check it on the portal before filing. Web/PWA: the regulations define the Aadhaar Verifiable Credential as a UIDAI-signed document that 'may contain' the last 4 digits, name, address, gender, date of birth and photograph, shared in full or part with an OVSE (Reg 2(be)), verifiable with or without offline face verification (Reg 3A). Third-party descriptions of the Aadhaar App describe portable SD-JWT credential sharing, and one integrator's public guide distinguishes an APP channel (app-to-app) from a WEB channel (browser redirect) and states that on iOS 'redirecting to Aadhaar app and completing Aadhaar validation as part of OVSE flow is not supported as of now'. So: request signing and the callback live server-side (a Convex HTTP action); the cross-device QR (admin's screen, worker's phone) is the path to build; same-phone web-to-app from an installed PWA is unsupported on iOS today and a pilot test on Android. Masked Aadhaar: the Secure QR is defined as UIDAI-signed data carrying the last 4 digits, demographics and photo (Reg 2(bc)), so masking does not break verification; Reg 16B(1) and 16C(1) require an OVSE to verify UIDAI's signature in the Secure QR before accepting Aadhaar in any form, and the 2025 amendment removed m-Aadhaar and XML from that list. For the pilot do not build a parser or accept card uploads: the admin validates in person with UIDAI's own scanner app and records only name, last 4 digits, a QR-verified flag, date and admin ID. Storing the Aadhaar number is barred (Reg 14A(b); Reg 20A(1)(d) even for optional logs; Act s.29(4) against public display; Act s.40 penalty up to 3 years, Rs 10,000, or Rs 1 lakh for a company). Because Act s.7/s.8 and Reg 5(1)(c) require alternatives to be offered and disclosed, driving licence, voter ID and PAN must be accepted in any case. Refined chain: apply the same person-check to the owner or authorised signatory of every business role, including pre-processors, compounders, DWCC/MRF operators, brands, authorised waste handlers and TSDFs; their entity-level checks (GSTIN, KSPCB consent or authorisation, EPR registration) are a separate admin checklist. Decision unchanged: verify with driving licence, voter ID or PAN (DigiLocker once live), accept Aadhaar only as an in-person Secure-QR check with UIDAI's app, store last 4 digits and a flag, apply for OVSE now on the cross-device QR pathway.

verdicts.question: How does a private company onboard as a DigiLocker requester through API Setu (process, cost, timeline), and can an NGO's attestation stand in for ID for undocumented migrant waste pickers under KYC-style verification?
verdicts.problems: Method note: verified through GitHub mirrors and snippets only (WebSearch exhausted, fetches refused). CONFIRMED: the Partners SOP exists at the cited URL and is MeitY's SOP for onboarding issuers and requesters via API Setu covering identification, evaluation, verification, agreement, technical integration, testing, launch and support (a KYC reference site labels it 'DigiLocker-Partner-SOP-2024'); Setu's own docs repo confirms sandbox dg-sandbox.setu.co, production dg.setu.co and 'Contact Setu for providing the credentials', with no pricing; the RBI KYC Master Direction updated 14 Aug 2025 (mirror) defines OVD as passport, driving licence, proof of possession of Aadhaar, voter ID, NREGA job card and NPR letter, defines a Small Account by PML Rules r.9(5) and says it is 'operational initially for a period of twelve months which can be extended for a further period of twelve months'; the Rs 1 lakh credits / Rs 10,000 withdrawals / Rs 50,000 balance limits appear in mirrored Direction text; two searches of the Aug 2025 mirror for 'gazetted' returned nothing, consistent with the claim that the gazetted-officer letter is no longer in the Direction; the NAMASTE guideline wording 'recent receipts from sale of scrap, endorsement by scrap shop owners / other registered Waste Pickers' or membership of a recognised organisation, followed by ULB validation, is confirmed via a secondary research mirror; the same mirror confirms e-Shram needs Aadhaar plus an Aadhaar-linked mobile plus a bank account (31.89 crore registrations as of Aug 2026). NOT CONFIRMED by any snippet: the SOP date 5 June 2024, the weekly onboarding committee, CEO approval, the 3-month deletion of unverified accounts, the STQC audit and quarterly usage reports; the Requester Terms of Use clause 'Currently, there are no platform charges applicable' (2 June 2025), which is the whole cost answer; Requester API v1.12 / Meri Pehchaan v2.4; the NeGD 3-fiscal-year provider rule; NamoID's 'long pole'; the Medianama 25 Sep 2026 report and the 21 Sep 2026 Request for Empanelment; the Civilsdaily 1.52 lakh enumeration figure; Citizen Matters (BBMP stopped issuing cards, 15 Sep 2025); 30 Stades 10,437 cards; the 2014 RBI press release. GAP the researcher under-weighted: the NAMASTE mirror says the MIS issues the ID only 'after ULB validation and e-KYC', and that resource organisations must assist e-KYC, so a worker with no Aadhaar may not reach a NAMASTE ID inside the proposed 90-day path; the provisional tier needs an explicit 'no Aadhaar yet' branch (enrolment help, not just a referral). Refined chain: the answer treats Saathis only; the signatories of the new business roles (pre-processors, compounders, DWCC/MRF operators, TSDFs) should go through the same DigiLocker/PAN person-check, and a provisional (attestation-only) Saathi should be barred from custody of hazardous-stream lots (e-waste, batteries, tyres, used oil, S1-S2 states) as well as cash, since those may move only to authorised handlers. No arithmetic to check.
verdicts.correction: Route: DigiLocker requester access is granted by NeGD (MeitY) through the API Setu partners portal under MeitY's Partner Organisation Onboarding SOP (2024), which covers identification, evaluation, verification, agreement, technical integration, testing, launch and ongoing support for issuers and requesters. The researcher's further detail (official-domain email, Entity Locker verification with the nodal officer's Aadhaar OTP, weekly onboarding committee, CEO approval, signed Requester Terms, demo, STQC audit and quarterly reports, deletion of unverified accounts after 3 months) comes from the SOP and portal pages that could not be re-confirmed here; treat it as the likely shape and confirm on the portal. Cost: the researcher reports the Requester Terms of Use (June 2025) say there are currently no platform charges; this could not be confirmed from any snippet, so budget zero but ask the onboarding team in writing; the DSC, engineering and any audit are your costs. Timeline: no official SLA; plan several weeks to a couple of months. For a 13 Oct start use a TSP: Setu's docs give a sandbox (dg-sandbox.setu.co) and production (dg.setu.co) with credentials issued by Setu and no public pricing, or run manual checks, and apply directly in parallel. NGO attestation: under the RBI KYC Master Direction (updated 14 Aug 2025) an OVD is a passport, driving licence, proof of possession of Aadhaar, voter ID, NREGA job card or NPR letter; no gazetted-officer or NGO letter appears in the current Direction; the only banking fallback is the Small Account (credits up to Rs 1 lakh a year, withdrawals up to Rs 10,000 a month, balance up to Rs 50,000; 12 months, extendable by 12 if an OVD has been applied for). RBI KYC does not bind Luma's own verification because the pilot moves no money and Luma is not a regulated entity. Official precedent for occupational attestation exists: NAMASTE lets CSOs profile waste pickers with 'recent receipts from sale of scrap, endorsement by scrap shop owners / other registered Waste Pickers' or membership of a recognised organisation, after which the ULB validates; but the NAMASTE MIS issues the unique ID and photo card only after ULB validation and e-KYC, so a worker without Aadhaar needs enrolment help first, and e-Shram needs Aadhaar plus an Aadhaar-linked mobile plus a bank account. So: an attestation from a recognised waste-picker organisation (Hasiru Dala) or a verified kabadiwala plus an admin-taken photo supports a capped provisional Saathi tier with an expiry (no cash custody, no custody of hazardous-stream lots such as e-waste, batteries, tyres or used oil, pickups paired with a verified partner) and a 90-day path that includes Aadhaar enrolment support where needed, then NAMASTE or e-Shram; it never substitutes at the payment layer, where the bank's own KYC applies. Claims that BBMP stopped issuing occupational cards and that 1.52 lakh pickers were enumerated nationally are unconfirmed here; ask Hasiru Dala and the city NAMASTE nodal officer. Refined chain: run the same DigiLocker/PAN person-check on the signatories of pre-processors, compounders, DWCC/MRF operators and TSDFs, separately from their entity-level checks. Decision unchanged: apply for direct requester access now, use a TSP for day-one DigiLocker if needed, treat attestation as a capped provisional tier with counsel's sign-off on the tier and DPDP notice before 13 Oct.
